chunks: 4636 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbbād ibn Ṣuhayb, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

There is no harm in looking at the hair of the women of Tihāmah, the Bedouins, and the people of the desert from among the People of the Covenant, and the non-Arabs, because when they are forbidden, they do not refrain.
He said: And the overpowered madwoman—there is no harm in looking at her hair and body, so long as that is not done deliberately.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: the protected non-Muslim communities under covenant
key_terms.الْمَجْنُونَةُ: a madwoman or mentally unsound woman
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal blame
key_terms.يَتَعَمَّدْ: to do something deliberately or intentionally

ai.seo_question: When does this hadith say there is no harm in looking at a woman’s hair or body?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling about cases in which looking at uncovered hair or body is not considered blameworthy under specific social circumstances. It also states a condition regarding the mentally overpowered woman, namely that such looking is not to be intentional.
